title: Virumaandi
overview: A film that narrates the same story from two opposing perspectives in a village and prison setting, directed by Kamal Haasan.
cast: Kamal Haasan, Pasupathy, Abhirami, Napoleon
review: Critically acclaimed for its narrative style and socially relevant themes including capital punishment and caste conflict.

title: Enthiran
overview: Dr. Vaseegaran, a brilliant scientist, creates an android humanoid robot named Chitti to serve humanity. However, when Chitti begins to experience human emotions, chaos ensues as the boundaries between man and machine blur.
cast: Rajinikanth, Aishwarya Rai Bachchan, Danny Denzongpa, Santhanam, Karunas
review: A landmark in Indian cinema for its groundbreaking visual effects and scale. Rajinikanth’s dual performance and Shankar’s ambitious direction make it a sci-fi spectacle that redefined Tamil film production values.

title: Super Deluxe
overview: An irreverent, multi-threaded story of an unfaithful wife, a father returning home, a transgender man, and a boy wanting revenge — all whose lives collide in one fateful day in Chennai.
cast: Vijay Sethupathi, Fahadh Faasil, Samantha Akkineni, Ramya Krishnan
review: Praised as one of Tamil cinema’s boldest films of the decade, noted for its dark humour, ensemble cast and genre-blending narrative.

title: Chennai 600028
overview: A coming-of-age sports comedy that follows a group of young men from Chennai who bond over their love for street cricket and friendship, facing challenges, rivalry, and love along the way.
cast: Jai Sampath, Shiva, Premji Amaren, Aravind Akash, Nithin Sathya
review: A cult classic that redefined youth-based Tamil cinema, known for its realistic portrayal of friendships and Yuvan Shankar Raja’s energetic soundtrack.

title: Jigarthanda
overview: An aspiring filmmaker sets out to make a movie about a ruthless gangster, but his research brings him dangerously close to the real-life world of crime and morality.
cast: Siddharth, Bobby Simha, Lakshmi Menon, Karunakaran, Guru Somasundaram
review: A genre-bending dark comedy and crime thriller. Bobby Simha’s performance won a National Award, and Karthik Subbaraj’s storytelling was widely acclaimed.

title: Kaithi
overview: A recently released prisoner races against time to save the lives of unconscious police officers while yearning to meet his daughter for the first time.
cast: Karthi, Narain, Arjun Das, George Maryan, Dheena
review: A gripping, high-octane action thriller told in real time. Critically acclaimed for its tight screenplay, emotional depth, and lack of songs — a rare move in Tamil cinema.

title: Amaran
overview: A biographical action war drama directed by Rajkumar Periasamy, based on the life of Major Mukund Varadarajan. The story follows his journey in the Indian Army and the impact it has on his family and legacy.
cast: Sivakarthikeyan, Sai Pallavi, Bhuvan Arora
review: Widely praised for its emotional core and production scale, Amaran emerged as one of the top grosses of 2024.

title: Aayirathil Oruvan
overview: An adventurous expedition leads a team of archaeologists and porters deep into a forgotten civilization, uncovering shocking secrets about history, power, and identity.
cast: Karthi, Reemma Sen, Andrea Jeremiah, Parthiban
review: A cult fantasy-adventure epic known for its ambitious storytelling, haunting music, and bold visual style — considered ahead of its time in Tamil cinema.

title: Meiyazhagan
overview: A heartwarming tale of friendship and emotional bonds set against a rural Tamil Nadu backdrop, exploring love, loss, and personal transformation.
cast: Kamal Haasan, Jayam Ravi, Siddharth, K. S. Ravikumar, Nithya Menen
review: Critically acclaimed for its soulful narrative, emotional depth, and stunning cinematography. Ghibran’s music and Kamal Haasan’s performance were especially praised.

title: Ratsasan
overview: A psychological crime thriller about a filmmaker-turned-cop who tracks down a brutal serial killer targeting schoolgirls, leading to an intense cat-and-mouse game.
cast: Vishnu Vishal, Amala Paul, Radha Ravi, Kaali Venkat
review: Widely regarded as one of the best Tamil thrillers of the decade, praised for its gripping screenplay, haunting score, and chilling realism.

title: Kaakha Kaakha
overview: A dedicated police officer’s life takes a violent turn when he takes on a deadly criminal gang, and his duty clashes with his newfound love.
cast: Suriya, Jyothika, Jeevan, Daniel Balaji
review: A stylishly made action thriller that redefined Tamil cop dramas. Known for its gripping screenplay, strong emotional core, and iconic chemistry between Suriya and Jyothika.

title: Kadaisi Vivasayi
overview: The story of the last active farmer in a small village who refuses to abandon his land and traditions, reflecting on humanity’s disconnection from nature.
cast: Nallandi, Vijay Sethupathi, Yogi Babu, Raichal Rabecca
review: A poetic and soulful film celebrated for its authenticity and minimalism. Nallandi’s performance and Manikandan’s direction earned universal acclaim and multiple awards.

title: Pariyerum Perumal
overview: A law student from an oppressed community faces caste discrimination and social injustice while holding onto his dreams and dignity.
cast: Kathir, Anandhi, Yogi Babu, G. Marimuthu, Lijeesh
review: A powerful social drama that became a milestone in Tamil cinema for its raw realism and strong anti-caste message. Critically acclaimed and emotionally resonant.

title: Kannathil Muthamittal
overview: An emotional drama set against the Sri Lankan civil war, about a young girl who learns she was adopted and seeks her birth mother.
cast: R. Madhavan, Simran, Nandita Das, Prakash Raj
review: Highly acclaimed and winner of multiple National Awards for its sensitive storytelling and technical excellence.

title: Aaranya Kaandam
overview: A neo-noir gangster film about a day in the lives of multiple criminal factions, whose turf war and drug deal go horribly wrong in one night.
cast: Jackie Shroff, Ravi Krishna, Sampath Raj, Yasmin Ponnappa
review: Won multiple National Awards including Best First Film of a Director; now regarded as a cult Tamil film.

title: Aandavan Kattalai
overview: Aandavan Kattalai is a Tamil satirical drama film that follows Gandhi, a man from a small village who tries to obtain a passport and visa by falsifying his documents, leading to a series of humorous and thought-provoking events about morality, immigration, and integrity.
cast: Vijay Sethupathi, Ritika Singh, Pooja Devariya, Nassar, Yogi Babu
review: A gentle yet sharp social satire with an engaging screenplay and stellar performance by Vijay Sethupathi. Praised for its realism and humor, it stands out as one of the best Tamil films of 2016.

title: Anbe Sivam
overview: A journey of two contrasting men — a cynical ad-director and an idealistic union man — where through unexpected events they discover humanity and sacrifice.
cast: Kamal Haasan, Madhavan, Kiran Rathod
review: Now regarded as a classic of Tamil cinema, noted for its philosophical depth and emotional impact.

title: Pithamagan
overview: A man raised in a graveyard with minimal human contact makes an unlikely friendship with a con-man which changes both their lives.
cast: Vikram, Suriya, Laila, Sangeetha
review: Praised for haunting performances by Vikram and Suriya, strong direction and a gritty narrative.

title: Paruthiveeran
overview: Set in rural Tamil Nadu, a rebellious young man’s romance with his cousin collides with family honour and village politics.
cast: Karthi, Priyamani, Saravanan, Ponvannan
review: A raw, realistic portrayal of village life; Karthi’s debut leaves a strong mark.

title: Kattradhu Thamizh
overview: A Tamil-MA graduate struggles to find meaning in life, faces societal rejection and spirals into existential despair.
cast: Jiiva, Anjali, Karunas
review: Lauded for its daring story, style and emotional intensity.

title: Subramaniapuram
overview: A gritty period drama set in 1980s Madurai: five friends engage in crime, betrayal and the harsh realities of small-town life.
cast: Jai, M. Sasikumar, Samuthirakani, Swathi
review: Marked a turning point in Tamil cinema for its realistic tone and storytelling.

title: Aadukalam
overview: In rural Madurai, cock-fights form the background for an intense tale of mentorship, rivalry and betrayal between a veteran trainer and his protégé.
cast: Dhanush, Taapsee Pannu, Kishore, V. I. S. Jayapalan, Naren
review: Won six National Film Awards including Best Director and Best Actor; widely regarded as one of the modern Tamil cinema classics.

title: Soodhu Kavvum
overview: A dark-comedy crime film about a gang of inept kidnappers who find themselves in over their heads when a politician’s son complicates their job.
cast: Vijay Sethupathi, Sanchita Shetty, Karunakaran
review: Praised for its humour, originality and cult appeal; became a standout film of 2013 in Tamil cinema.

title: Anjaathe
overview: Satya and Kiruba are friends growing up playing together; while Kiruba studies hard to become a sub-inspector, Satya’s life is aimless. When Satya unexpectedly becomes a police officer, the balance between them shifts, leading to betrayal, violence and emotional catastrophe.
cast: Narain, Prasanna, Ajmal Ameer, Vijayalakshmi
review: Anjathe was widely praised for its gritty style, technical ambition and ability to balance mainstream thrills with art-house sensibility. It remains a key film in the Tamil new-wave movement.

title: Visaaranai
overview: A group of Tamil laborers in Andhra Pradesh are arrested and brutally tortured for a crime they did not commit, exposing the corruption and abuse within the police system.
cast: Dinesh, Samuthirakani, Anandhi, Ajay Ghosh, Kishore
review: A raw, hard-hitting drama based on real events. Won three National Awards and was India’s official entry to the Oscars in 2016. Highly acclaimed for its realism and emotional depth.
